### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **8** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **145** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**103** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`, `recordId (4 routes)`
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (symbol, 51 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 51 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **197** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `83630250852e359866794bb6761ff69f366b33fa` — the merge of head `efbf75c0352fc21b9d096c68c10544176c93ffd1` into base `25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 83630250852e359866794bb6761ff69f366b33fa && git checkout 83630250852e359866794bb6761ff69f366b33fa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f efbf75c0352fc21b9d096c68c10544176c93ffd1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f && git merge --no-ff efbf75c0352fc21b9d096c68c10544176c93ffd1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `efbf75c0352fc21b9d096c68c10544176c93ffd1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/feed.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-body-doors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts + packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-doors.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/script-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/core/src/security/caller-mail-bounds.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/outbox-sender-bound.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/app-activity-door.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ScriptCapabilitiesField.tsx

Inputs read: issue #32004 (body and all 21 comments), PR #32966 (body, comments 6840737853 and 6840743876, the 81-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge-base `1a6c3309`), and the check-runs on the head as of 2026-11-13T01:26Z. Read outside the diff, not reviewed: the engine's read options and hook session (`packages/objectql/src`), the permission-set resolver and the authorization middleware (`plugin-security`), the mail service and the `sys_email` object, the activity stamp hook, `scripts/check-spec-parsed-alias.mjs`, `packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts`. Tests, the changeset text, `docs/**`, `content/docs/**`, generated files and translations are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Findings are graded M (must-fix), S (should-fix), N (nit). Part of M1, two should-fix findings and two notes are held by the lane seat and are not written in this record; their grades count in the verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `HookBodyCapability` gains `email.send` and `activity.append`. Right. It is one accept set, read by the `capabilities` array of a hook, action and job body, and it only widens. Declared equals enforced on all three faces: the VM checks the token before it reads the input or reaches the host seam (`installDoor`, `throwCapabilityDenial` never returns), and a host built without kernel services answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
2. `BodyDoorRecordRefSchema`, `BodyMailSendInputSchema`, `BodyActivityAppendInputSchema`, their three types and `BODY_MAIL_RECIPIENT_LIMIT` are new exports of `@objectstack/spec/data`. Right as additions. Every object is `.strict()`, so a stamped key is refused, not dropped, and the PR body's `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` sentence holds. `requiredOneOf(['text', 'html'])` is an arm of the closed projectable list, so the body rule reaches the published JSON Schema. Wrong in two respects: the published schema does not state the 50-recipient total (S1), and several strings carry no upper bound (S4).
3. `SYS_ACTIVITY_PLATFORM_TYPES` is a new constant. Right. `satisfies` holds it to a subset of `SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES`, which is unchanged, so the writer census is not owed. The column's vocabulary stays open: the door refuses ten values and admits every other.
4. `ExtractedBody.capabilities` on `@objectstack/cli/hook-body` widens in output position. Right: the ratified union in `published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts` moves with it and the changeset names it.
5. `@objectstack/core` gains `boundCallerMail`, `mailAddressOf`, `isPlainMailObject`, `SENDER_HEADER_NAMES` and three types. Right, additive. `@objectstack/rest` keeps `SENDER_HEADER_NAMES` by re-export. The REST door's bounds were read against `main` sentence by sentence: same order (`sentBy`, `headers`, `from`, `organizationId`, `identityMail`), same texts, same forwarded message. "The REST door's answers are unchanged" holds.
6. `sys_activity.origin` is a new read-only column. Right, additive.
7. `AppArtifactHandlerBindingOptions.getService`, `ScriptContext.email` and `ScriptContext.activity` are optional additions to the runtime's public types. Right.
8. `plugin-email`: an outbox row the mail service did not write has its `from_address` replaced by the configured sender before it lands, and emptied where none is configured. This is no accept-set change. It changes what an existing direct insert sends; see ② and ③.
9. `plugin-security`: a notice only, once per elevation kind and object, and no refusal. Right against ruling 6796076408 ("until step 3 lands, elevated automation's inserts into append-only objects are not judged").
10. Check-runs on the head: 44 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 12 still running. Every lint, build and gate job is green, including `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three finished `Type Check` jobs and `Live E2E UI`. Pending, not judged: `Test Core` 1/8, 3/8, 7/8 and 8/8; `Test UI` 1, 6, 9, 10, 13 and 16 of 16; `Type Check UI`; `Type Check · workspace`.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` takes `minor`: right. `Metadata-protocol: added` is the right kind (two new accepted values an author can write), and a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves.
- The other eight packages take `patch`: right by AGENTS.md step 3 (a non-protocol change ships `patch`).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right for the accept sets, and both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset.
- The PR body carries no `Skills-docs:` line. A kind other than `none` owes one. The lane seat settles it before ACCEPT.
- The changeset ships the outbox sender bound as a `patch` line with no BREAKING banner. It takes the choice of sender away from a row an app inserted itself. Whether that is a breaking behaviour change is the lane seat's reading at ACCEPT, together with the escalation in ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The PR body declares no open question. The two declared deviations are judged in ④.
- Escalated, rule text. On #32004 the only rule text for this step is ruling 6796076408 (2026-11-11T12:40Z; the brief dates it 2026-11-09), read with 6787890900. It says: one door sends mail through the mail service, and the other appends to the timeline through a platform door that stamps the actor and the provenance. No step design beyond that is on the issue. The 50-recipient cap, the hourly limit and its environment variable, the platform-only type list, the reserved metadata keys, the outbox sender bound and the deprecation notice stand on the PR body alone. The lane seat names where the maintainer approved them, or puts them to the maintainer.
- Escalated, step order. The ruling puts first-party apps onto the doors in step 2 and judges inserts only in step 3. The outbox sender bound changes what a direct insert sends in step 1, before any app has moved. The maintainer confirms that it belongs to step 1, or it moves.
- Open question for step 2. The deprecation notice also fires for a flow's system identity and names two body doors. A flow has no door of its own in this diff; it reaches one only through an action it calls.
- Check-runs: 12 pending, listed in ①.10. This verdict does not rest on them.
- The PR is a draft with no auto-merge armed, so no disarm is owed. Its author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

Deviation (a): the 50-recipient total is held in the runtime door, and the schema caps each slot. Acceptable as built. `recipientCount` counts a bare address as one and a list by its length, over all three slots, before anything is read or sent, and the schema's `max` bounds each list. The sum has no exact JSON Schema spelling, so it cannot join the closed projectable list. One gap follows, S1.

Deviation (b): the hourly limit counts every `sys_email` row of the organization in the last hour, so a job's sends count too. Acceptable as built. It is the conservative direction, it is read from the shared log so every node sees one count, and a job is the sender a volume limit most needs to cover. The code agrees with the PR body's sentence where the caller has an organization. Mail the door did not send (the HTTP door, other services) counts toward the number and is never refused by it, so that mail can close the door; identity mail is in its own log and is not counted. See N4.

**M1 (must-fix), `body-runner.ts` `hookDoorCaller`.** On the hook face the door does not read the pointed-at record in the caller's scope. `readContext` is `executionContextFromHook(engineCtx)`: four fields copied from the hook session (`userId`, `tenantId`, `positions`, `isSystem`). That function's own docblock calls it "the closest scope reachable on this path rather than a copy of the read path's". The read door judges a caller by the permission-set names its context carries (`resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized` reads `context.permissions`), and `invitation-placement.ts` records that a hand-built context resolves "to the additive baseline and NOTHING else". The hook session carries no `permissions`. So the record is judged against a grant set that is not the caller's, and a record the caller reads through an assigned permission set is answered `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. The PR body's sentence, "a record the call points at must be one the caller can read", is therefore not what the hook face holds. The action face is right: `callerScopeOf` hands back the caller's own envelope with the body's elevation removed. The hook face owes the same scope, built by the same function from the context of the operation that fired the hook. The hook test (`body-doors-capability.test.ts`) runs on a `ql` double that ignores the context, so no test reads through the real door.

**S1 (should-fix), `hook-body-doors.zod.ts`.** The published surface does not state the recipient total. `BodyMailSendInputSchema`'s description, its JSON Schema and the generated reference page carry the per-slot `max` and nothing about the sum, so a document they accept is refused by the door. That is the direction `refinement-projection.ts` calls silent. State the total where the published schema is read: in the schema's `.describe()` text, or as a declared refinement whose site the dropped-refinement ledger names on the artifact.

**S2 (should-fix), `quickjs-runner.ts` `installDoor` and `body-doors.ts`.** A door call does not ride a transaction the body opened. `installDoor` never reads `txState`, and the host seam reads and writes through the root engine with contexts that carry no transaction handle. The engine's own docblock says a VM body's `ctx.api.transaction` handle is threaded explicitly and is invisible to the ambient store. The neighbouring `ctx.title` seam reads `txState.api` at call time for this reason, and its comment records the cost of not doing so: a second connection, and a deadlock on a one-connection pool, the `objectstack dev` default. On a driver with transactions, a door call inside `ctx.api.transaction` therefore cannot read a record the body just wrote, and its timeline entry stays when the body rolls back. Ride the open transaction, or refuse a door call inside one with a sentence that says so.

**S3 (should-fix), `app-artifact-handlers.ts` and `body-runner.ts` `installBodyDoors`.** The package part of `origin` is the binder's `appId` for every group. The binder groups each package body's hooks and actions under that package's own id (`hookBindingGroups`, `actionBindingGroups`), but builds one body runner per bundle with the bundle's `appId`. In a bundle that carries `packages[]`, `origin` names the bundle and not the package that holds the body, and two packages' bodies of one name stamp the same origin. The column's description and the PR body both say the package. Jobs take the same `appId`.

**S4 (should-fix), `hook-body-doors.zod.ts`.** `subject`, `replyTo`, an address's text, `type`, `recordLabel`, `object`, `id` and the size of `metadata` carry no upper bound; only `summary` does. On the timeline side every `sys_activity` field is read-only, so the record validator bounds none of its columns and the door is the only place a bound can sit. A bound added after this schema is published is a narrowing. Decide the bounds now.

**N1 (nit), `hook-body-doors.zod.ts`.** `BodyMailSendInput` and `BodyActivityAppendInput` read `z.infer`; ADR-0122 gives the author-state name to `z.input`. The two shapes coincide today. `check-spec-parsed-alias.mjs` treats a name ending in `Input` as not bare, so the gate is green and neither schema is pinned isomorphic. Write both as `z.input` and pin them, as the diff does for `BodyDoorRecordRef`.

**N2 (nit), `feed.zod.ts`.** The docblock of `SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES` still tells an author that "an app's server-side action can insert one directly". This diff deprecates that insert and adds the door. Name `ctx.activity.append` there.

**N3 (nit), `body-doors.ts` `callerScopeOf`.** For an absent context it answers the system scope. No caller in this diff passes one. An exported function named for the caller's scope should answer a scope with no principal.

**N4 (nit), `body-doors.ts` `refuseOverHourlyLimit`.** A caller with no organization is counted against the whole log, and the refusal still says "this organization's mail log". Say which count was read.

**N5 (nit), `outbox-sender-bound.ts`.** The docblock says a row with no configured sender is stored with the column empty and fails at delivery. `sys_email.from_address` is `required`, so the insert itself may be the refusal. Not measured; make the sentence match what happens.

Files that hold as written: `hook-body.zod.ts` and `index.ts` (①.1, ①.2); `feed.zod.ts` apart from N2; `caller-mail-bounds.ts`, `core/src/security/index.ts` and `rest/src/email-routes.ts` (①.5); `script-runner.ts`; `app-plugin.ts` (all three runner sites and the artifact binder pass the service lookup); `app-activity-door.ts` (the platform-only types, the reserved metadata keys, the excluded objects and the append-only bucket are refused before the row is built; the actor snapshot is the platform's; the row is written under a plain system context that carries no automation mark, as the ruling's "platform's ledger writer" item requires); `audit-plugin.ts`; `sys-activity.object.ts`; `flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts` and `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` (①.9); `extract-hook-body.ts` (an under-inferred token is a sandbox refusal at run time, the closed direction, as for `log` and `crypto`); `ScriptCapabilitiesField.tsx`. `outbox-sender-bound.ts` and `email-plugin.ts` do what their sentence says for `from_address`: field defaults are applied before `beforeInsert`, so a row that omits `status` is seen at `queued`, and a batch is dispatched one row at a time.

M1 is a FAIL. The fixes of M1 and S1 to S4, and of the findings the lane seat holds, earn a delta review by this reviewer on the new head.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cx5nHfga3Hm9BzikGw`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
